payload.artist_html: G. Mayr, L. Šmídová, A. Richter & S. Wedmann
payload.credit_html: "Evidence for diurnal habits in an exceptionally preserved Eocene owl"
payload.description_html:
Details of the feet of Masillastrix and other Eocene Strigiformes:

(A–D) M. blattophaga, detail of the left hallux (A) to show the short phalanx (dotted line), and left foot/leg in plantar (B and C) and dorsal (D) views; (C) and (D) are micro-CT images (all SMF-ME 11964A except C, in which images from both slabs were combined); the circled area in (B) denotes a detail of the tibiotarsus to illustrate the immature condition of the individual; the black arrows in (D) indicate the joints between the pedal phalanges. (E) M. blattophaga, right foot. (F) Palaeoglaux artophoron from Messel (SMF-ME 1144A), right foot. (G) Minerva cf. leptosteus from the early Eocene of Wyoming, USA (AMNH 29000), left tarsometatarsus. (H) Ypresiglaux michaeldanielsi from the early Eocene London Clay (NMS.Z.2021.40.26), right tarsometatarsus and pedal phalanges.

Specimens in (A), (B), and (E) were coated with ammonium chloride. The toes are numbered; the white arrows in (A), (E), and (F) delimit the first phalanx of the hallux. fem, femur; fib, fibula; flg, plantar flange formed by tarsometatarsal trochlea for fourth toe; flx, flexor tubercle; tbc, tubercle; tbt, tibiotarsus; tmt, tarsometatarsus. The scale bars represent 10 mm.
